questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
It has been a valuable experience in some respects, but many of the courses have not been useful, and the level of instruction was not based on legislation or legal principles, but rather on theory and personal opinions. I am not sure whether this was because I simply chose the wrong subjects.

In general, the school itself was not well-structured. The mandatory attendance requirements create significant pressure, and absences require a medical certificate. All exams are handwritten and without any aids, which makes little sense to me. Moreover, the teaching was often disorganised and unclear, making it difficult to understand what the lecturers were saying or expecting. We were frequently informed only a few days in advance that we had to prepare presentations, and at times we were assigned more than 30 pages of reading to complete within less than two days.

The most concerning issue is that we may not receive our grades until 17 January, which poses a serious problem, as I am scheduled to start as a junior associate on 1 January.
